pilot.final_answer:
## Results: Good-Value Wine Regions

After scanning 130k wine reviews across the UMAP projection and probing 12 candidate regions, I was unable to find four regions that simultaneously meet the acceptance thresholds (intent_match ≥ 0.75, purity ≥ 0.70) for good-value wines (≥90 points, ≤$40). The search was stopped after two consecutive rounds yielded no new relevant themes.

Here's what I found, ranked by strength of evidence:

---

### 1. Old World Reds with Structure and Value ⭐ (Best Finding)
**Region:** scan-3 | **Purity:** 0.75 | **Intent Match:** 0.65 | **Projection Agreement:** 0.85

This is the strongest candidate. It captures structured, earthy Old World reds — primarily **Austrian Blaufränkisch** and **Spanish Tempranillo/Tinto Fino** — with dark fruit, firm tannins, and excellent quality-to-price ratios. Three of four sampled wines met both the ≥90-point and ≤$40 criteria. The one outlier was an Italian blend at $50. This region represents a genuine value sweet spot in the projection.

---

### 2. Good-Value Wines (Mixed French Reds & American Chardonnay)
**Region:** scan-1 | **Purity:** 0.50 | **Intent Match:** 0.60 | **Projection Agreement:** 0.875

A dense but thematically split region. Two sub-themes coexist: **French red wines** and **American Chardonnay**. Two of four sampled reviews met the quality-price criteria, while one lacked pricing and one exceeded $40. Refinement into four sub-regions failed to purify the signal — the children degraded into mixed reds, overpriced wines, dessert/fortified wines, and generic whites, all with intent_match ≤ 0.30. This region has good-value wines but they're interleaved with other content.

---

### 3. Crisp, Fruity White Wines Under $30
**Region:** scan-6 | **Purity:** 0.85 | **Intent Match:** 0.55 | **Projection Agreement:** 0.95

Thematically coherent — crisp, fruity, ready-to-drink white wines — but only one of four sampled wines (a Mosel Riesling) met the 90+ point threshold. The others scored 84–89 points. This region represents **value pricing** but not the high-quality tier requested. High projection agreement (0.95) gives confidence in the spatial placement.

---

### 4. Good-Value White Wines (Ripe & Creamy)
**Region:** scan-5 | **Purity:** 0.80 | **Intent Match:** 0.30 | **Projection Agreement:** 0.85

Thematically pure — white wines with ripe fruit and creamy textures, positively reviewed for value — but only one of four hit 90+ points. The quality threshold is the main failure. This region is a genuine value cluster, just at a slightly lower quality tier than requested.

---

### Caveat

No region reached the acceptance threshold. The projection appears to cluster good-value wines more by style and price than by the specific intersection of high quality (90+) *and* moderate price (≤$40). The strongest signal (scan-3, Old World reds) is worth exploring further — Austrian Blaufränkisch and Spanish Tempranillo appear to be reliable value categories. The white wine value clusters (scan-5, scan-6) are coherent but skew toward 86–89 point wines rather than 90+.
